title: The Health Autonomy Journal: John's results, retest by retest
description: Osteopath John Evans tracks his own Health Autonomy results in Chudleigh, Devon: VO2 max, BodyAge, muscle, body fat, heart, lungs, power and steps, with honest monthly updates.
headline_html: Practising what we preach. Every result, in public.
lede: I ask patients to measure, act and retest. So I’m doing the same: the same six tests, the same equipment, retested every 8 weeks, with honest updates on what I’m changing and what’s working.
numbers_intro: Results from the Health Autonomy assessment, retested every 8 weeks on the same equipment, plus my average daily steps each month. Each card shows the latest result and how it has changed since the first test.
updates_intro: A short update each month: training, sleep, nutrition, steps, what’s working and what isn’t.

follow.heading: How I’m working towards my targets
follow.text: My targets are the numbers above: a fitter heart and lungs, more muscle, better balance. The everyday work behind them, mostly strength sessions, walks and easy runs, goes on Strava. Follow along to see what it takes week to week; my updates below say how it’s going.

updates.title: My baseline: what the numbers say
updates.body_html:
I had my baseline assessment on 26 October. It was the same tests any Health Autonomy client has, on the same equipment. Overall, I’m pleased. My estimated fitness, resting heart rate and body composition all came out where I’d want them. The AGE Reader put my BodyAge at 41, against my actual age of 48.

The tests also showed me what I need to work on: my left and right sides don’t share the load equally. On the force plates, my left leg did 11% less of the work when pushing off in a jump. Standing on my left leg, my balance was noticeably shakier than on my right. My right arm also carries a little less muscle than my left. With my injury history, I’m not surprised. But it’s exactly the kind of thing you’d never spot without measuring.

My plan for the next 8 weeks

  • Single-leg strength twice a week: split squats, step-ups and single-leg deadlifts, always starting with my left side.
  • Balance work most days: a few minutes standing on one leg, eyes open and then closed. Brushing my teeth is a good time for it.
  • Single-arm presses and rows, so my right arm can catch up.
  • Keeping my walks and easy runs going, so my fitness doesn’t slip.
  • Retest just before Christmas, with the same tests and the same equipment.

I’ll post an update each month. When I retest, the cards above will change, whether the numbers go the way I want or not.

updates.title: The starting line
updates.body_html:
I’ve been an osteopath for 20 years, and I’ve spent a lot of that time telling people that stiffness, weakness and poor balance aren’t just “getting older”. Most of it can be improved. I created Health Autonomy to prove it, and this journal is me putting myself through exactly what I ask of patients.

I know recovery first-hand. After acute brachial neuritis and spondylolisthesis, I rebuilt my fitness and went on to complete the Roc Triathlon adventure race in Wales. Now I want to see what the numbers say.

This month I’m taking my baseline assessment: body composition, AGE Reader, ECG, heart rate variability, spirometry and force plates. My results will go up here as soon as I have them, good or bad, followed by my plan for the next 8 weeks.
